summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old male with a history of kidney transplantation, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, coronary artery disease, and peripheral vascular disease was readmitted for worsening dyspnea on exertion, chest pressure, and lower extremity swelling. He had been recently discharged after treatment for volume overload and DVT. Evaluation revealed acute on chronic diastolic heart failure with volume overload, confirmed by elevated BNP, chest X-ray findings, and physical exam. He was treated with IV furosemide, transitioned to oral torsemide 60 mg daily, and had his medications optimized, including holding irbesartan, increasing tacrolimus, and bridging with heparin due to subtherapeutic INR. Cardiac catheterization showed chronic total occlusion of the RCA and mild LAD disease, not requiring intervention. Carotid ultrasound revealed complete right internal carotid artery occlusion and 60–69% stenosis on the left. He was stabilized, educated on low-salt diet, and discharged home with follow-up plans in cardiology, vascular surgery, and transplant nephrology.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease

Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris
Occlusion and stenosis of bilateral carotid arteries
